title: Risk-adjusted reserved GPU credit sculpting + fallback guarantee packaging experiment
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Objective: design and validate a new packaging variant that combines reservation credits with an SLA-backed fallback guarantee and a risk-adjusted sculpting model for enterprise buyers. This ticket drives an experiment to compare three commercial arms: 1) Classic Reserved Ladders (fixed GPU SKU tiers + monthly commit), 2) Sculpted Credits (commit -> flexible credit pool that converts to GPU-hours with diminishing marginal discounts), 3) Hybrid Reserve+Burst (soft reserve + metered burst with per-minute overage pricing and automatic fallthrough to a lower-cost model variant). The product needs to be supported by contract language and security questionnaire answers for enterprise RFPs.
background_and_rationale: Sales feedback and recent closed-won postmortems indicate deals stall on two axes: perceived over-commitment risk and lack of capacity fallthrough guarantees. Large customers want predictable unit economics but also assured availability during peak windows. Current reserved SKUs are simple but brittle: customers either overcommit (wasted spend) or undercommit (risk of throttling). We propose a sculpted credit model that smooths commitments and a legally-backed fallback guarantee that falls back to a compatible model family or regional capacity with defined RPO/RTO and cost differentials.
experiment_design: Arms: A- Reserved Ladder (control), B- Sculpted Credits (experiment), C- Hybrid Reserve+Burst (experiment). Duration: 12 weeks pilot with 6 enterprise prospects negotiated by Sales Engineering. Success metrics: conversion uplift (trial -> committed) >= 12% vs control; average monthly utilization of reserved capacity >= 65%; net MRR delta positive; reduction in sales cycle length by >= 10 days. Pricing knobs: discount cliffs at 3/6/12 month commitments, sculpting elasticity factor (alpha), burst overage multiplier, preemption-credit refund policy. Instrumentation: per-deal telemetry in Console (route, SKU usage, overage events), tagging for pilot customers, updated contract clause stored in Drive: /Enterprise/Contracts/Reserved-Playbook/PM-427665.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pricing bands defined and tabled for Sales on Confluence; 2) Legal-approved fallback SLA clause drafted and included in master SOW template; 3) Pilot instrumented such that Console shows per-customer reserved utilization and burst events; 4) Sales closes at least 4 pilot deals within experiment window OR internal simulations meet revenue/usage thresholds; 5) Security questionnaire template updated to include KMS/HSM options, data segmentation assurances, and audit log retention language.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-offs considered: heavier flexibility (sculpted credits) reduces churn risk but increases billing complexity and forecasting variance. Hybrid Reserve+Burst simplifies forecasting but requires robust bursting metering and preemption rules; it also pushes engineering to tighten autoscale and region failover behavior. We prioritized commercial simplicity for initial pilot (clear discount bands + conservative burst rate) and will iterate pricing elasticity after first 6 pilot closes. Revenue recognition impacts were reviewed with Finance; sculpted credits are treated as deferred revenue per existing policy.
